gw_in_ikev2.legacy_note: The Kaskad CA certificate is of the old kind: a device that trusts it accepts its signature for any site. Replace it (kaskadctl gw pki rotate ikev2 or “Gateway → Protocols → IKEv2”) and reissue the IKEv2 settings.
gw_in_ikev2.ca_where.windows: the Kaskad CA certificate is inside the kaskad-ikev2.ps1 script, no separate file needed
gw_in_ikev2.ca_where.apple: the Kaskad CA certificate is inside the kaskad-ikev2.mobileconfig profile
gw_in_ikev2.ca_where.file: the Kaskad CA certificate, file kaskad-ikev2-ca.crt
gw_in_ikev2.err.no_host: IKEv2: the client address (gateway.host) is unknown — the server certificate needs it: kaskadctl gw host <address or name> or gw host --detect.
gw_in_ikev2.err.no_certs: IKEv2 certificates aren’t created yet: kaskadctl gw apply.
gw_in_ikev2.ca_scope: The Kaskad CA vouches only for this server ({host}): it isn’t valid for other sites.
gw_in_ikev2.ca_purpose: The device uses it to verify the server.
gw_in_ikev2.how.ios: Open the file on the iPhone or iPad → Settings → “Profile Downloaded” → “Install”.
gw_in_ikev2.how.macos: Open the file → System Settings → General → Device Management (macOS 13–14: Privacy and Security → Profiles) → “Install”.
gw_in_ikev2.mobileconfig_note: The profile contains the device’s password — give the file only to the user it was issued to.
gw_in_ikev2.ps_trust: The script adds the Kaskad CA certificate to the computer’s trusted root certificates.
gw_in_ikev2.linux_note: Package charon-cmd; it asks for the password itself.
